This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:

On 19.12.2018 at about 7.00 pm., when the petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA- 18-Y-5100 slowly cautiously by observing all traffic norms (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.1468/2019 on the said road, at that time, all of a sudden a Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-A-2920 which was driven by its driver at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner dashed and against the said motor cycle.

Due to tremendous impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on his body and was immediately shifted to Government Hospital, Ajjampura after first aid treatment he was shifted to Max Hospital, Shimoga wherein treated as outpatient and from there shifted to NIMHANS and from there shifted to Fortis Hospital, Bangalore wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and from there shifted to Nano Hospital wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
He is still bed ridden and was under treatment and has spent nearly Rs.25,00,000/- towards medical and nourishment expenses.
He has to undertake further treatment and has to incur future medical expenses also.
The petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The petitioner has suffered loss of income due to (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.1468/2019 this accident.
The accident occurred due to the reckless driving of the driver of the Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-A-2920.
In this regard a case has been registered by Ajjampura police and has also registered a case against the driver of the vehicle.
The first respondent is the insurer and second respondent is the owner of the vehicle.
Hence, both are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner constrained to file a petition and sought for awarding Rs.1,50,00,000/- as a compensation.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court, remained absent hence, placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal and filed their written statement.
The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts of the same.

It has contended that, respondent is the insurer of Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-A-2920 and (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.1468/2019 liability to indemnify the 2nd respondent is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, provisions of the MV Act, valid and Yogeshappa N.M vs Iffco Tokio General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56715838/

sentences.text: It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further it has contended that, complaint has lodged after lapse of 3 days from the date of alleged accident.

It has contended that, the rider of the motor cycle not having driving licence to drive the vehicle, the injured took the risk of riding the motor and this is clear case of "Volunti non fit injuria" and the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of petitioner himself.
It has denied the age, avocation, income and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner.

The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exaggerated,
excessive, arbitrary etc.,
With these grounds the respondent No.1 sought for rejecting the claim (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.1468/2019 petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 19.12.2018 at 7.00 pm., was riding the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-18-Y-5100 slowly cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations near Anuvanahalli village road, Chikkamagaluru, at that time, all of a sudden a Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-A- 2920 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the said motor cycle.
Due to the tremendous impact the said petitioner fell down and he sustained grievous injuries as on the date of alleged accident ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award?
5.

In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1, one medical record Incharge at Fortis Hospital has examined as PW.2, Manager at Nano (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.1468/2019 Hospital has examined as PW.3, one witness from medical record department, NIMHANS has examined as PW.4, Dr.Sharan Srinivasan has examined as PW.5, one eye witness has examined PW.6, One Neuro surgeon, Fortis Hospital has examined as PW.7, Head constable, Ajjampura police has examined as PW.8 and one Investigating Officer has examined as PW.9 and in all got marked Ex.P.1 to 22.

10. I have perused Ex-P1 to Ex-P18.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 19.12.2018 at about 7.00 pm., and the FIR in crime No.0330/2018 came to be registered on 22.12.2018 at 19.00 i.e., after lapse of 3 days after the accident at (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.1468/2019 Ajjampura Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC and 187 of MV Act.
Further the records reveal that, know person of petitioner has lodged the complaint.
IMV report marked at Ex.P.2 reveals that damages caused to the vehicles bearing reg.No.KA-50-M- 2920 and KA-18-Y-5100.
It also reveals, the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defect of the motor vehicles.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW-1 i.e., wife of petitioner.
I have perused the entire cross-examination of PW-1.

In her cross- examination she has specifically denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 that, the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of petitioner himself and produced created documents.
Respondent No.1 has contended that, complaint was lodged after lapse of 3 days from the date of accident.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 - FIR and complaint, the alleged (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.1468/2019 complaint was lodged on 22.12.2018 whereas accident occurred on 19.12.2018 as there was delay of 3 days and at complaint it has mentioned that, due to lack of knowledge to the wife of petitioner,
complainant has lodged the complaint on 22.12.2018.

As per Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 ACJ 911 (Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and others), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting claim application".

In that reported case, injured was the minor boy sitting on the side of the road in front of his house,
accident was witnessed by the father of the injured and another person and they took the injured to the hospital, next day police came to the hospital but no FIR was recorded as father of injured was under mental agony and stress and he was more concerned to get the medical treatment to his son.
In that case, complaint was lodged (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.1468/2019 after 3 months of the accident.
Considering the facts and situations of that case, their Lordships held that delay in lodging complaint cannot be a main ground for rejecting the application.

From going through the averments in the complaint and the facts in the present case on hand, immediately after the accident, injured was shifted to Government Hospital, Ajjampura after first aid shifted to Max hospital, Shimoga and then to Fortis Hospital.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.

It has also held that, Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Therefore, delay in lodging the complaint is not a ground to reject the petition.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve the version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet - Ex.P.4 filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Moreover, it is settled law

that the term "rashness and Yogeshappa N.M vs Iffco Tokio General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56715838/
5 negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence driver of Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-A-2920 which belongs to the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:
In view of answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering, sustained by (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.1468/2019 the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc. let me discuss one by one:
a) Towards Injury, Pain and Suffering: PW.1 has contended that due to accident her injured husband was sustained grievous injuries like traumatic head injury with left fronto temporal craniotomy status, traumatic left burst temporal lobe with left fronto temporo partial extradural and subdural and subdural hematoma with mass effect and mid line shift and injuries to other parts of the body.
In order to prove injuries caused to him, PW.1 has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P8 wherein doctor has opined injury is grievous in nature.

The record shows that the petitioner took treatment in the hospital as an inpatient and he has examined one medical record incharge as PW.2 and produced documents such as (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.1468/2019 authorisation letter and 3 case sheets which are got marked at Ex.P.13 and 14.
Petitioner has also examined Manager at Nano Hospital, Bangalore and through him got marked Authorisation and case sheet marked at Ex.P15 and 16.
Petitioner has also examined Medical Record Keeper at NIMHANS and got marked Ex.P.19 and 20.
Petitioner has examined Dr.Sharan Srinivasan as PW.5 and got marked NPBA report at Ex.P.21 and OP record at Ex.P.22.
One witness by name Mahanthesha has examined as PW.6.

Dr.
Sachin.G.R, Neuro Surgeon at Fortis hospital has examined as PW.7.
Head constables at Ajjampura police station has examined as PW.8 and PW.9.
PW.4 has assessed the petitioner for disability.
Therefore by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.75,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.1468/2019 claimed compensation towards medical expenses.

Pw.1 contended that immediately after the accident her injured husband was shifted to Government hospital, Ajjampura after first aid treatment he was shifted to Max Hospital, Shimoga wherein took treatment as outpatient, again he was shifted to Fortis Hospital, Bangalore wherein he took treated as inpatient from 20.12.2018 to 05.02.2019.

PW.1 has produced 111 medical bills amounting to Rs.18,32,696.18/- marked at Ex.P.9 and 30 medical prescriptions and also produced 9 medical bills amounting to Rs.25,100/- marked at Ex.P.17 and 33 deposit receipts marked at Ex.P.18.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not disputed reagarding the medical bills and expenses incurred by the petitioner towards Yogeshappa N.M vs Iffco Tokio General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56715838/
6 treatment.

sentences.text: Hence, in all the Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,57,796/- which is rounded off to Rs.18,57,800/- is just and reasonable towards Medical expenses.

c) Towards food, extra nourishment,
Conveyance and medical attendant charges: Petitioner has produced 3 discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.5 to 7.

On perusal of the same, Ex.P.5 is the discharge summary issued by Fortis Hospital wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 20.12.2018 to 05.02.2019 i.e., for 47 days, Ex.P.6 is the discharge summary issued by Nano Hospital which reveals petitioner took treatment from 05.02.2019 to 18.02.2019 i.e., for 13 days, Ex.P.7 is the discharge summary issued by NIMHANS wherein he took treatment from 30.05.2019 to 31.05.2019 ie., for 2 days, in total petitioner took treatment for 62 days.
Therefore, it is considered as that the petitioner took treatment for 62 days.
During the time of treatment the petitioner also required healthy food and extra nourishment.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 62 days and also by including conveyance, a sum of (SCCH-9) 18 MVC.No.1468/2019 Rs.1,00,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.
d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment:
PW.1 has contended that he was working as Village Accountant at Shivani Madakacheri, Ajjampura and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But in this regard she has not produced any document.
In the absence of positive documents regarding petitioner's occupation and income this Tribunal will consider notional income.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2018 at 12,500/-
p.m.,
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2018 treated as Rs.12,500/- p.m.

Considering the age, nature of injuries, treatment given & duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 4 months.
Thus, by taking into account the notional income of PW.1, this Tribunal (SCCH-9) 19 MVC.No.1468/2019 awards Rs.50,000/- (12,500/- X 4) towards loss of income during treatment period.

e) Towards Loss of Income due to Functional Disability: PW.1 has examined Dr.Sharan Srinivasan as PW.5 he has deposed that at the time of evaluation he was found to be unconscious with a come score of 7T/15, he was also found to have right sided paucity of movements (weakness of limbs due to brain injury).

A CT scan revealed a large contusion in the left temporal and frontal regions (blood clot within the brain), small contusions in the right side of the brain, EDH in the left frontotemporal region and SAH (blood clots deep inside the brain) with diffuse Yogeshappa N.M vs Iffco Tokio General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56715838/
7 edema and midline shift.

sentences.text: All these were suggestive of severe injury to both sides of the brain.

He underwent an emergency left FTP decompressive craniotomy &
evacuation of the contusion on 20.12.2018.

Postoperatively, he was managed with mechanical ventilator, injections to control fits, infection,
brain (SCCH-9) 20 MVC.No.1468/2019 swelling and cerebral cell activators and protectors.
A tracheostomy was done, he was diagnosed to have a life threatening condition called 'pulmonary embolism'.
Further PW.5 deposed that, he continued to be in altered sensorium and discharged on 05.02.2019.
At the time of discharge from NIMHANS on 11.04.2019 as an emergency.
A CT scan had revealed dilated ventricles( fluid collection in the brain due to the severe head injury).
A right VP shunt was done on same day and discharged on the same day.
His come score was 9A/15 at discharge.
Again on 30.05.2019 he was admitted for a titanium cranioplasty on 31.05.2019 and was referred to rehab on 27.06.2019.
Further deposed that, he has assessed for the brain related disabilities on 27.02.2020 about after 2 years of accident.
A detailed clinical evaluation revealed a conscious but dull patient, with very poor verbal comprehension.

He has spastic right hemiplegia and petitioner advised to undergo detailed neuro rehab (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.1468/2019 assessment and neuro psychological and behavioral assessment but on attempt to assess, could not be done due to severe verbal comprehension issues.
After about 3 years, on 23.01.2021 he has been assessed for disability.

He had made a marginal motor recovery wherein it reveals that, petitioner able to walk with a stick in his left hand and one person support, tried to eat with left hand but spills, recognizes only close relatives, still has no urine control, still needs support for all ADL and spastic right hemiplegia still present.
PW.5 further deposed that, all the disability due to the severity of the brain injury and permanent disability.

PW.5 further deposed that, the modified rank in scale (MRS) is a commonly used scale for measuring the degree of disability or dependence in the daily activities of people who have suffered a stroke or other caused of neurological disability and his MRS grade is 4 - Moderately severe disability.
PW.5 assessed 80% disability and based on all (SCCH-9) 22 MVC.No.1468/2019 these data and detailed evaluations, his functional disability is 100% irrespective of occupation.

The learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon citation reported in 2020 SCC Online Kar 1446 (Alameli Bai Vs. Managing Director, KSRTC) wherein it is held that, even in case of functional disability cases, future prospects can be awarded.

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the amount towards future prospectus.
PW.1 produced Aadhar card of petitioner marked at Ex.P.11 which reveals that, petitioner was born in the year 1958 and the accident occurred on 19.12.2018.
Hence, it is clear that, as on the date of accident petitioner was aged 60 years.
As per Sarala Verma's Case the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is "09".
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioner is entitled for additional 10% of income to the future prospectus.
So, the total gross income of deceased is Rs.13,750/- per month (12,500 + 1,250).
Thus petitioner (SCCH-9) 23 MVC.No.1468/2019 is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,85,000/- = (13,750 x 12 x 9 x 100%) towards loss of future income due to permanent disability.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the Insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

14. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of .36,17,800/-

Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said  compensation amount, 25% shall be  (SCCH-9) 27 MVC.No.1468/2019 deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification through e-payment.

Draw up award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
On 19.12.2018 at about 7.00 pm., when the petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA- 18-Y-5100 slowly cautiously by observing all traffic norms (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.1468/2019 on the said road, at that time, all of a sudden a Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-A-2920 which was driven by its driver at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner dashed and against the said motor cycle.
The petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred due to the reckless driving of the driver of the Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-A-2920.
The first respondent is the insurer and second respondent is the owner of the vehicle.
Hence, both are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It has contended that, respondent is the insurer of Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-A-2920 and (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.1468/2019 liability to indemnify the 2nd respondent is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, provisions of the MV Act, valid and Yogeshappa N.M vs Iffco Tokio General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56715838/
2 effective driving licence held by the driver of Car, valid permit, RC, FC.
It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It has contended that, the rider of the motor cycle not having driving licence to drive the vehicle, the injured took the risk of riding the motor and this is clear case of "Volunti non fit injuria" and the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of petitioner himself.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exaggerated,
excessive, arbitrary etc.,
The learned counsel for petitioner has submitted citations reported in:
a) (2011)4 SCC 693 b) 2013 Kant MAC 3 (kant)
Yogeshappa N.M vs Iffco Tokio General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56715838/
3 c) 2022 ACJ 170 (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.1468/2019 d) ILR 2003 KAR 493 e) MFA 7493/2007(MV)
f) 2016 ACJ 1976 g) MFA 2667/2008 (MVC)
h) ILR 1996 Kar 161 i) MFA 11380/08 (MV-Ins)
j) 2011 ACJ 1 k) 2005 ACJ 644 l) AIR 2018 SC 1347 m) III (2013) ACC 424(SC)
n) MVC 2510/2020 (Injury case future prospects)
The learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon citation reported in 2020 SCC Online Kar 1446 (Alameli Bai Vs. Managing Director, KSRTC) wherein it is held that, even in case of functional disability cases, future prospects can be awarded.
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and passing through severity of the brain injury and permanent disability.
Petitioner is unable to attend to own bodily needs without assistance and unable to walk unassisted.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 19.12.2018 at 7.00 pm., was riding the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-18-Y-5100 slowly cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations near Anuvanahalli village road, Chikkamagaluru, at that time, all of a sudden a Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-A- 2920 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the said motor cycle.
Due to the tremendous impact the said petitioner fell down and he sustained grievous injuries as on the date of alleged accident ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, delay in lodging the complaint is not a ground to reject the petition.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet - Ex.P.4 filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Moreover, it is settled law
that the term "rashness and Yogeshappa N.M vs Iffco Tokio General Ins Co Ltd on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56715838/
5 negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.75,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
Hence, in all the Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,57,796/- which is rounded off to Rs.18,57,800/- is just and reasonable towards Medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the amount towards future prospectus.
Hence, it is clear that, as on the date of accident petitioner was aged 60 years.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioner is entitled for additional 10% of income to the future prospectus.
So, the total gross income of deceased is Rs.13,750/- per month (12,500 + 1,250).
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable to under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
g) Towards future medical expenses: The doctor/PW5 has not opined about the future medication of the petitioner.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head future medical expenses.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus petitioner (SCCH-9) 23 MVC.No.1468/2019 is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,85,000/- = (13,750 x 12 x 9 x 100%) towards loss of future income due to permanent disability.
12. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 (SCCH-9) 24 MVC.No.1468/2019  Sl. Particulars Amount
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the Insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being the Insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
14. Issue No.3:
In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of .36,17,800/-
 (Rupees thirty six lakhs seventeen thousand eight hundred only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
In the event of deposit of the said  compensation amount, 25% shall be  (SCCH-9) 27 MVC.No.1468/2019 deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
